datasets.name: Computational 2D Materials Database (C2DB)
datasets.description: DFT and many-body properties of monolayer crystals, with experimental-derived and generated candidates.
datasets.count_scope: Version table entry dated 2024-05-01, not the stale introductory description.

sources.title: C2DB official release history
sources.evidence: Release table lists 16,789 rows for 2024-05-01; full dataset is provided upon request.

caveats: The overview still says around 4,000; the release table is more recent.
Full download requires an author request; browsing is public.
Legacy CMR declares CC BY-SA 4.0 globally, but current 2DHub release-specific data license was not verified.

datasets.name: van der Waals Bilayer Database (BiDB)
datasets.description: Stacked homobilayers with DFT interlayer energies and detailed properties for the stable subset.
datasets.count_scope: All stacking configurations in the 2024 study; detailed labels for 2,586 stable bilayers.

sources.title: BiDB official page
sources.evidence: 8,451 homobilayers are constructed from 1,052 monolayers; 2,586 stable bilayers have expanded labels and an ASE database is linked.

caveats: Count includes multiple stackings of the same monolayer, not 8,451 distinct chemistries.
C2DB-derived monolayers overlap the parent family.

datasets.name: van der Waals 2D Heterostructure Database (HetDB)
datasets.description: Relaxed heterobilayers selected for commensurability, small strain and tractable cell size.
datasets.count_scope: Official database description viewed 2026-11-01.

sources.title: HetDB official page
sources.evidence: 336 heterobilayers from 44 monolayers are relaxed with PBE-D3; cells have fewer than 300 atoms and in-plane strain below 1%.

caveats: Selection excludes large mismatch or large supercell combinations.
Count is bilayer combinations, not independent monolayer chemistries.

datasets.name: Quantum Point Defects Database (QPOD)
datasets.description: Intrinsic point defects in monolayers across charge states, with electronic and optical properties.
datasets.count_display: 2,061 rows representing 500 distinct intrinsic point defects
datasets.count_scope: Release table lists 2,061 rows; distinct defects are counted separately.

sources.title: QPOD official page
sources.evidence: 500 distinct intrinsic defects are evaluated in multiple charge states; version table lists 2,061 rows.

caveats: Rows include different charge states; do not report them as 2,061 distinct defects.
Derived from C2DB host materials.

datasets.name: Materials Cloud Two-Dimensional Structure Database (MC2D)
datasets.description: Computational exfoliation of experimentally reported layered bulk crystals, with AiiDA provenance.
datasets.count_scope: 2022.84 archive contains 3,077 extracted structures, not all DFT optimized.

sources.title: MC2D archived release
sources.evidence: Archive contains 3,077 extracted structures, 2,710 optimized structures and 2,345 electronic band structures.

sources.title: MC2D record metadata
sources.evidence: File license is CC BY 4.0.

caveats: Bulk sources include ICSD, COD and MPDS; derived structures may overlap other 2D databases.
The 3,077 count is broader than the optimized or easily exfoliable subsets.

datasets.name: 2DMatPedia
datasets.description: Top-down exfoliation of Materials Project layered parents and bottom-up chemical substitution.
datasets.count_scope: Official 2019 Figshare JSONL archive, independently counted 6,351 parseable records.

sources.title: 2DMatPedia official Figshare metadata
sources.evidence: Version 3 releases monolayer structures and properties under CC BY 4.0.

sources.title: 2DMatPedia official JSONL data
sources.evidence: Downloaded JSONL contains exactly 6,351 parseable structure records; local SHA-256 retained.

sources.title: 2DMatPedia author paper
sources.evidence: Top-down screening and bottom-up element substitutions produce the monolayer collection.

caveats: Generated substitutions are not experimental materials discoveries.
Overlap with Materials Project and other monolayer collections requires structure-level checks.

datasets.name: JARVIS-DFT 2D snapshot
datasets.description: NIST monolayer materials subset with optB88-vdW and related calculated properties.
datasets.count_scope: Actual d2-12-12-2022.json.zip payload linked by current jarvis-tools.

sources.evidence: v8 metadata declares CC BY 4.0 and links the dated 2022 archive.

sources.evidence: Documentation reports 1,109 for dft_2d, differing from the linked archive.

caveats: Named subset of JARVIS; do not add its count to the entire JARVIS family.

datasets.name: CoRE MOF Database
datasets.description: Experimental-derived MOF structures curated for simulation and classified for structural validity.
datasets.count_display: 43,439 full-family records; 9,256 openly deposited SI structures
datasets.count_scope: Full 2025 family across SI, CSD-modified and CSD-unmodified branches; includes CR and NCR.
datasets.license: CC BY 4.0 for Zenodo SI deposit; CSD-derived files have additional CCDC access terms

sources.title: CoRE MOF 2025 v1.0
sources.evidence: Full family 43,439 = 9,256 SI + 21,009 CSD-modified + 13,174 CSD-unmodified; SI has 2,737 CR and 6,519 NCR entries. CSD update is marked not updated.

sources.title: CoRE MOF 2024 release history
sources.evidence: Prior family had 40,837 records and 8,300 SI structures. ASR/FSR duplicates and a recommended unique screening list are documented.

sources.title: CoRE MOF 2025 deposit metadata
sources.evidence: The SI file deposit declares CC BY 4.0; CSD branches have separate access terms.

caveats: Ranked count is the full mixed-access family; the open SI subset has 9,256 structures. The full family is not wholly computation-ready.
Public 2025 SI contains 9,256 structures; modified CSD files require email registration and unmodified CSD files a CCDC license.
2025 deposit labels the CSD branches not updated; verify distribution before using those counts as available downloads.
ASR and FSR variants can derive from the same original structure; use the release-specific recommended screening list.

datasets.name: Quantum MOF Database (QMOF)
datasets.description: Periodic DFT structures and electronic properties for MOFs and coordination polymers.
datasets.count_scope: Current author README lower bound; no exact current row count inferred from older papers.

sources.title: QMOF author repository
sources.evidence: Current author README describes 20,000+ MOFs and coordination polymers, CC BY 4.0 data, and no trajectories.

sources.title: QMOF official Figshare metadata
sources.evidence: Current version is 18 with CC BY 4.0 data; separate QMOF-Thermo archive is present.

caveats: 20,375 is a historical widely cited count; later release notes removed individual structures, so it is not asserted as the current exact count.
Includes experimental-derived and hypothetical MOFs; overlaps CoRE, Boyd-Woo and other MOF families.
QMOF-Thermo is separately packaged and not added into this structure count.

datasets.name: Wilmer hypothetical MOF database (hMOF)
datasets.description: Combinatorial assembly of MOF building blocks with computed pore and gas-storage properties.
datasets.count_scope: Original Wilmer et al. corpus, not a filtered JARVIS or MOFX mirror.

sources.title: Wilmer et al., Nature Chemistry
sources.evidence: Original study generated 137,953 MOFs from 102 building blocks and calculated pore and methane-storage properties.

sources.title: Author-hosted original paper
sources.evidence: Author paper confirms 137,953 generated structures from 102 building blocks.

caveats: Count is historical; downstream exports can contain fewer structures, including the NIST hMOF mirror.
Original portal access and an explicit reusable data license were not established in this audit.
Generated geometries do not establish synthesis or thermodynamic stability.

datasets.name: Boyd-Woo hypothetical MOFs for wet flue-gas capture

datasets.count_scope: Full Materials Cloud release described by the 2019 archive.

sources.title: Boyd-Woo Materials Cloud archive
sources.evidence: Deposit contains 324,426 hypothetical MOFs; more than 8,000 received refined simulations. MEPO-QEq charges are provided.

sources.title: Boyd-Woo file rights
sources.evidence: Release metadata declares CC BY 4.0.

caveats: ARC-MOF and QMOF reuse some structures from this family.
Charge-generation validation is not proof of synthesizability.
Only the refined subset has the higher-fidelity calculations.

datasets.name: ab initio REPEAT Charge MOF Database (ARC-MOF)

sources.title: ARC-MOF rights metadata

all_structures archives describe the larger candidate universe; they are not additive ARC-MOF structures.

datasets.name: MOSAEC MOF Database (MOSAEC-DB)

datasets.name: CURATED covalent organic frameworks

datasets.name: Open Direct Air Capture 2025 (ODAC25)

resources.name: MOFX-DB
resources.description: Adsorption-data portal aggregating experimental and hypothetical MOFs, COFs and zeolites. Source datasets overlap CoRE, hMOF, ToBaCCo and IZA; portal totals are not additional unique structures.

sources.title: MOFX-DB primary descriptor
sources.evidence: Describes computational adsorption datasets across multiple source families and thermodynamic conditions.

queries: C2DB official release history and license
IZA framework code count PCOD SLC good

limitations: No material total should be computed by summing these heterogeneous and overlapping records.

Source verification was primary-provider or primary-author based. Several pages were fetched through official REST APIs when rendered pages hid licensing; hashes are retained under evidence-specialized.
Explicit data licenses remain unverified for some 2DHub projects, legacy hMOF/PCOD/IZA, X23/ICE13, BEAST and the SAC portal. A paper or software license was not silently applied to raw data.
The documented numeric count is deliberately a dated release/subset when live counts are unavailable. OC20/OC22/OC25/ODAC/OMC/Zeo-1 count frames, IZA counts topology types.
JARVIS 2D archive independently contains 1,103 records despite documentation 1,109. Public OMC25 train+val totals 26,257,042 frames despite full-paper27M+ description.
DigCat current provider count differs from the requested ACS Perspective >500k computational claim; no unique-material count or exact release behind that claim was independently verified.
Broader 2D materials such as Alexandria2D belong to the root inorganic-family audit; NOMAD and Materials Cloud are aggregators recorded separately by the root.
Additional recent resources worth future verification include LitMOF-DB, OC20NEB/AQCat25, zeolite adsorption configurations, MOF stability datasets and private molecular-crystal prediction corpora.
